verdict.rationale: Official docs describe Grok Bot apps for both iPhone and Android, used to start work, answer questions, approve steps, review results, share content via the iOS share sheet, and continue threads across phone and desktop. However, the documented mobile scope is a subset of the desktop experience rather than clearly full-featured, and one hands-on report says GitHub login on iOS was broken, which prevented use. Missing for 10: evidence of feature parity with desktop (e.g., Agent Computer view, bot management, skills/routines on mobile), Android-specific feature documentation, and independent corroboration that the mobile apps work reliably (the iOS login failure goes unresolved).

support.subject: As a knowledge-worker, I can use full-featured official mobile apps for iOS and Android

citations.quote: Use Grok Bot on iPhone or Android to start work, answer questions, approve steps, and review results away from your desk.
On iPhone, use the system share sheet and choose Grok Bot to send a photo, file, link, or text into a chat.
You can message a Bot from your phone or desktop, the way you would text someone on your team, and pick up the same thread later on either surface.
